- Current standing: you are evaluating Redwood for a pilot around our patient-scheduling assistant and want to make sure contract language and operational controls meet your compliance bar.

Proposed next steps: 
1) I attached the list of your questions from the call (Oakridge_DPA_Questions.docx) — please confirm nothing is missing.
2) I will loop in our legal lead (Marissa) for DPA clarifications and any redline questions.
3) We can provide a redline of our standard DPA and a short summary of subprocessors and detection/notification timelines by EOD.
4) If that looks good, we can move to DocuSign and aim to have an executed DPA before a pilot kickoff the week of 6/7.

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@oakridgehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rios <elena.rios@oakridgehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps

Thanks Ben — great call. A couple of clarifying questions so we can route to our InfoSec and legal teams: 

1) Can you confirm the contractual roles: will Oakridge be the Controller and Redwood the Processor for the pilot scope?
2) We need a full list of subprocessors (and a mechanism for notice when you add new ones). Can you share the current list?
3) Breach notice: what is Redwood's SLA for notifying customers after a confirmed or suspected incident? We typically require 72 hours for initial notification and a 30-day incident report.
4) Data residency: can you guarantee data stays in the US (region-specific hosting) for our PHI-adjacent data?
5) Retention and logging: default retention for logs/telemetry, and whether we can set a custom retention policy per account.

If you could have legal respond to these directly that would be ideal. Copying our procurement lead is next if needed.

- Samir
Information Security Manager\Oakridge Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@oakridgehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elena Rios <elena.rios@oakridgehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-21T16:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA clarifications and next steps

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (legal) to provide the formal responses; below is a concise summary so you have immediate answers while Marissa prepares a redline: 

- Controller/Processor: Redwood would act as a Processor for customer data processed via our hosted API. Oakridge would remain the Controller for patient data collected/ingested by your application. We include this language in our standard DPA.

- Subprocessors: we maintain a published list of subprocessors (current examples: AWS (infrastructure), Google Cloud CDN, Sentry (error monitoring), Segment/Datadog for telemetry where enabled). We provide 30 days' advance notice for new subprocessors and a mechanism to opt-out in specific cases through contract terms. Full list and a link will be included in the redline.

- Breach notification: our standard commitment is initial notification within 72 hours of confirming an incident that impacts customer data, with follow-up reports as we learn more. We can align on a 30-day detailed incident report cadence in the contract.

- Data residency: hosted customers may pin to a region (US or EU) depending on plan; for PHI-adjacent workloads we recommend our US-only region deployment. We can document the option and any limitations in the DPA.

- Retention & logging: default retention for request/usage logs is 90 days, but we support custom retention settings for Dedicated/Private deployments and can contractually set retention for Hosted if needed. We also offer KV/prefix caching controls to avoid storing PII at rest by default.

Attaching: Redwood_DPA_Redline.pdf (draft redline) — Marissa will follow with the formal redline and legal notes.

Let me know the compliance contact at Oakridge and I will ensure Marissa includes them on the next update.

Best,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@oakridgehealth.com>, Elena Rios <elena.rios@oakridgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood DPA redline and responses to Oakridge questions

Hi Samir / Elena —

Thanks for the helpful list. I reviewed Ben's summary and attached an annotated redline of Redwood's standard DPA (Redwood_DPA_Redline.pdf). Key points to call out from legal: 

1) Roles: Confirming Redwood executes as a Processor and Oakridge as Controller for the processing activities scoped in the DPA (section 1.1).

2) Subprocessors: The redline includes the current subprocessor list and our standard notice process (we publish updates and provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors). If Oakridge has a specific vendor you cannot permit, flag it and we can discuss a carve-out or an alternative.

3) Breach notice: We commit to initial notification within 72 hours of confirming an incident affecting customer data and provide a detailed report within 30 days; these clauses are represented in sections 6.2 and 6.4 of the redline. If you need stricter SLAs we can discuss trade-offs or Dedicated deployment language.

4) Data residency & retention: The DPA allows for region-specific processing where available; we have US-only deployments for customers requiring that. Default logging retention is 90 days; we included a retention appendix that allows you to specify a shorter retention if required by policy.

5) Subprocessor liability & audits: we referenced SOC 2 Type II certification and provided our audit contact; for deeper evidence (on-site or shared reports) we can arrange an NDA and a compliance pack exchange.

Next steps: 
- Please review the attached redline and mark any provisions you want to negotiate.
- If the edits look acceptable, we'll send the final DPA via DocuSign (link below) and aim for signature in the next 5 business days.
